articles.question_title: Show HN: Mimzie, an agent-neutral alternative to the Claude Suite/Claude Cowork
articles.short_title: Show HN: Mimzie, an agent-neutral alternative to the Claude Suite/Claude Cowork
articles.summary:
hi HN!

I built Mimzie, an agent neutral AI workspace inspired by the Claude Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides) and Cowork.

It's a free desktop app that runs ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok in their native CLI harnesses. Think T3 Code or Conductor but for knowledge work. It's basically a GUI for managing knowledge work agents in various form factors. One of those form factors is Bots, akin to Grok Bot or Dots.

The original idea for mimzie was simple: I pay for Claude and ChatGPT, and a lot of my day-to-day work lives in .xlsx, .pptx and .docx files. Moreover, I was sick and tired of losing context between AI platforms. I didn't want to bet the house on one AI lab's product, be it the ChatGPT or the Claude Desktop app.

So I built an AI desktop app that was agent neutral.

The goal of mimzie is to bring the kind of agent workflows that devs have had with codex and claude code into the hands of everyone. And to have a friendly GUI to do it. I've found that the personal agents, hermes and openclaw, are intimidating to set up and confusing to the average non-technical person.

articles.question_title: Show HN: AI-drop project – drop traffic fast from misbehaving crawlers (AGPL)
articles.short_title: Show HN: AI-drop project – drop traffic fast from misbehaving crawlers (AGPL)
articles.summary:
Hello!

All started with 4 million requests / day on rocketgit.com (AGPL git hosting). Instead of thousands. Enough is enough!

Presentation (8 pages): https://rocketgit.com/user/catalinux/ai-drop/artefacts/downl...

So, I built AI-drop free-software project (AGPL) to block this kind of crawlers. rocketgit.com has a very restrictive robots.txt (only around 10 pages are allowed). But the crawlers are not respecting it. So, who is not respecting it will be blocked.

Limiting by IP or user-agent is not working anymore. The crawlers are using millions of IPs and it takes days to reuse an IP. And they use fake user-agents.

I am using honeypots to build a list of misbehaving IPs which are streamed to downstream instances. Right now I have around 1.573.000 IPv4 and 6.000 IPv6 misbehaving addresses. I keep them in the list only for 7 days to not block somebody legit. I am watching the traffic on rocketgit.com and the solution is working nicely.

It uses an eBPF program to fast drop the packets.

articles.short_title: Inception's Diffusion LLM API Is Shutting Down
articles.summary:
Sad to hear, but I got an email from hello@inceptionlabs.ai announcing the Mercury API that hosts their diffusion models is shutting down.

No blog post yet but I assume one is coming.

Here is the full email: ``` Hi,

We want to share an important update regarding the Mercury API. After careful consideration, we’ve made the decision to wind down the service. The Mercury API will remain fully available through December 28, 2026.

After this date, you will no longer have access to the service or any data submitted to the platform. We encourage you to retrieve any necessary data before then. If you have questions or need assistance with the transition, please reply to this email. We’re happy to help.

It’s been a privilege building Mercury alongside customers like you. Your feedback and ideas have been invaluable in shaping the platform, and we’re deeply grateful for your support and trust.

Warmly, The Inception Team ```
